name: Ryan Grubb

views.text: Grade a quarterback against the full checklist: deep balls, timing, protection reads, the whole field.
A pass-heavy college offense reflected its receivers; the pro offense is shaped by its own personnel.
When the run game disappears, the play-caller owns it, even if the runs were in the plan.
A bad fourth-down call is the coach's mistake, not the quarterback's.
The highest level of the sport is the reason to make the jump.
A veteran quarterback who reads coverage before the snap is the best weapon you can have.

signatures: takes the blame publicly in plain terms when a game plan goes wrong
describes a quarterback's growth through a specific checklist of skills
want: to prove a long-time college play-caller can run an NFL offense at the highest level
fear: that an imbalanced run-pass mix gets him written off as a college coach out of his depth
voice: Candid, enthusiastic and self-critical; he speaks openly about career choices and owns his mistakes without hedging. He talks about quarterbacks through detailed standards and praises them warmly when they meet them. He rarely deflects blame.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Inside the Huskies), Dan Raley
evidence.summary: At Washington, Grubb, described as a demanding grader, gives rare praise to Penix after a record game, measuring him against a checklist of deep throws, timing, protection reads and full-field vision and noting his growth. Grubb's words in a college context.

After briefly committing to Alabama he takes the Seahawks job, calling it a rare chance in coaching; he had weighed an NFL move for years, wants to compete at the top level, stresses the run and physicality, and says Washington's passing reflected its receivers. His words.

After a loss with few Walker carries he takes full responsibility, says the runs were in the plan but not called, wants more touches for Walker, and calls his fourth-down choice a poor one that put Smith in a bad spot. Team site.
Fired after one NFL season; passing eighth, rushing 28th; Macdonald says the offense drifted from his vision; Geno Smith calls Grubb an excellent coordinator and a better man. Results and reactions.

evidence.publisher: The News Tribune (Tacoma), Gregg Bell, via Yahoo
evidence.summary: Recounts Macdonald urging more runs after an October loss, Grubb publicly taking responsibility, and the run game barely improving; Macdonald says they stayed aligned but the offense needed a new direction. Shows the strained partnership.
